senses.gloss:
Tājad-bhaṅga (‘easily broken’) is apparently the name of a tree or plant in the Atharvaveda. The kauśika sūtra treats it as a compound word, and its commentator makes it out to be the castor-oil plant (eraṇḍa). Whitney, however, treats the expression as two separate words, and thinks that the passage means ‘may they be broken suddenly (tājat) like hemp (bhañga).’
Foot notes viii. 8, 3 (a battle hymn).
